First, we pull out the factor of $4$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8x-1}{4x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{8x-1}{4(x-\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{8x-1}{(x-\frac{3}{4})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ \frac{3}{4} & 8 & -1 \\  & ↓ & 6 \\  & 8 & 5\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8x-1}{(x-\frac{3}{4})} & =8+\frac{5}{(x-\frac{3}{4})}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8x-1}{4x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int (8+\frac{5}{x-\frac{3}{4}})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[8\int \text{d}x+5\int \frac{1}{x-\frac{3}{4}}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[8x+5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-\frac{3}{4}|]+C \\  & =2x+\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-\frac{3}{4}|+C.\end{aligned}
$$
